                                                                                                                                        5
Nutrient analysis of fruit and vegetables




Executive summary
The aim of this survey was to provide up to date nutrient composition data for fresh and
processed fruit and vegetables. The data for these food groups published in the Composition
of Foods Integrated Dataset and included in the National Diet and Nutrition Survey nutrient
databank were last updated in the 1980s. Since then, there have been increases in both the
range and varieties of fruit and vegetables commonly consumed in the UK and increased
globalisation of the food supply has resulted in some products that were previously seasonal
being widely available throughout the year. The samples selected were those fruit and
vegetables that are most commonly consumed or fruit and vegetables where there were gaps
in the data available and consumption was increasing. Commonly consumed processed fruit
and vegetable products were also included.

The results from this analytical survey will be incorporated into the Department of Health’s 1
nutrient databank that supports dietary surveys and will be also be disseminated via the
authoritative UK food composition tables, McCance and Widdowson’s The Composition of
Foods.

This project reports analysis of 59 composite samples that were made up of between 9 and 22
sub-samples that were representative of fruit and vegetables consumed in the UK. Sub­
samples included were based on the need to take into account factors including cultivar, region
and country of origin and season. Fresh fruits and vegetables were sampled in two seasons
(summer/autumn and autumn/winter) where the cultivars and geographic origin were known to
change between seasons. Samples were purchased from retail outlets and prepared for
analysis between August 2011 and February 2012.

This sampling report gives details of the sub-samples making up each composite sample.
Analytical results from the survey are contained in a separate report. Results for individual
fatty acids are reported separately in electronic format.




                                                                                                 6
Nutrient analysis of fruits and vegetables




Sampling notes
•   Samples were collected according to a sample protocol produced in agreement with the
    Department of Health (DH).
•   Sub-samples were agreed with DH based on a review of market shares and nutrient
    content.
•   All samples were collected between August 2011 and February 2012 and stored according
    to usual consumer practice or according to packaging guidelines until required for
    processing.
•   Equal weights of each sub-sample were combined to complete the composite sample for
    analysis.
•   Sub-samples were stored at –20°C until required for further preparation. Composite
    samples were stored at -40°C before being sent to laboratories for analysis.
•   Where possible all sub-samples within a composite sample were prepared in a single day
    and the composite sample was produced on the same day. Where that was not possible,
    sub-samples were prepared and stored frozen until all sub-samples were available and the
    composite sample could be produced. Where sub-samples were purchased over two
    seasons, sub-samples from each season were prepared and stored frozen at -40 ºC until
    all sub-samples were available. Once all season samples had been collected they were
    thawed and mixed in equal proportions to produce the final composite sample.
•   Composite samples for analysis of vitamin C and folate in fresh fruit and vegetables
    consisted of sub-samples that were chopped into chunks and frozen immediately. Samples
    were delivered to the laboratory for analysis as soon as possible and were homogenised at
    the laboratory prior to analysis.
•   Ingredients, label claims and nutrient information presented in this report have been taken
    directly from product packaging.

 Sample Preparation
Purchased samples were stored according to packing guidelines and usual consumer
practices. Ambient products were stored at room temperature and chilled products were
refrigerated at 4ºC. Frozen products were stored at -20ºC and either thawed before use or
cooked from frozen, depending on product guidelines. Details of all sub-samples were
recorded prior to preparation of composite samples and all samples including packaging,
ingredient and nutrition information were photographed.

Where further sample preparation or cooking was required, samples were prepared according
to packaging instructions or based on guidance for consumers provided by a range of sources
including industry trade associations. Equal weights of un-homogenised sub-samples were
combined to form single composite samples. The composite samples were homogenised as
thoroughly as possible and were split into sub-samples of approximately 100g each.
Composite samples were stored frozen at -40ºC before being sent to laboratories for analysis.
Where possible all sub-samples within a composite sample were prepared in a single day and
the composite sample was produced on the same day. Where that was not possible, sub­
samples were prepared and stored frozen until all sub-samples were available and the
composite sample could be produced. Where sub-samples were purchased over two seasons,
sub-samples from each season were prepared and stored frozen at -40 ºC until all sub­
samples were available. Once all sub-samples had been collected from both sampling points,
they were thawed and mixed in equal proportions to produce the final composite sample for
analysis of all nutrients except vitamin C and folate. Analysis for these labile nutrients was
undertaken at the time of seasonal sampling and subsamples were chopped into chunks and
frozen immediately. Samples were delivered to the laboratory for analysis of folate and vitamin
C as soon as possible and were homogenised at the laboratory prior to analysis.

Details for each sample are given below, including weight changes on cooking and edible
portion measurements.

Sample 30: Tomatoes (standard), grilled, flesh and seeds only

For each sub-sample, 8 tomatoes were taken from 2 packs. Stalks were removed and
tomatoes were rinsed in Analar water and dried before halving. Tomatoes were grilled
(medium-high) for 2-3 minutes with the cut side down, and then 4-6 minutes with the cut side
up. After grilling, the skins (and the harder ‘stalky core’ for subsamples 30.12-30.22) were
removed.

For subsample 30.9 the pack contained a mixture of sizes of tomatoes, including some cherry
tomato sized and these smaller tomatoes were not used.

A good range of ‘firm’ to ‘well done’ was achieved within and between subsamples, due to
differences in size, ripeness and top/bottom of tomatoes.
